$comment: Known-safe matches for the no-secrets rule. Every entry carries a reason and the engine refuses to load one that does not — an allowlist nobody can justify is the scanner being switched off one line at a time. Prefer a `literal` over a `path`: allowing a path allows everything that will ever be added to it.

allow.reason: Holds the detection patterns themselves; matching on them is the rule scanning its own source.
This file. Its entries are by definition strings the scanner matches.
Fixtures deliberately contain credential-shaped values so both outcomes of the rule are tested.
Documents the credential formats contributors must recognise, with worked examples.
Quotes example findings, including the credential shapes that produce them.
Integrity hashes are high-entropy by construction and are not credentials.
Checksums are high-entropy by construction and are not credentials.
Jest snapshots reproduce fixture values verbatim; the source file is scanned instead.
